items.title: Top Yen Forecaster Predicts 147 Per Dollar as Rate Gap Narrows
points: Now, the top dollar-yen forecaster in Bloomberg’s latest rankings sees the Japanese currency rallying toward 147 per dollar next year as Japan’s interest-rate gap with the US narrows.
While Parker sees the yen strengthening to around 155 by year-end before appreciating further, Bloomberg’s top forecaster in the previous quarter sees it weakening as far as 170 next year.
Parker expects the Bank of Japan to raise its benchmark rate from 1.25% to at least 2%, potentially 2.25%, a more aggressive outlook for tightening than much of the market expects.
The Federal Reserve, meanwhile, may raise interest rates once more in December before stopping at around the 4.00-4.25% range, according to Parker.
Japan’s consumer price index excluding fresh food and energy, a metric closely monitored by the BOJ as a gauge of underlying inflation, advanced 2.4% in September.
Parker said that a pickup to 2.6% or higher could prompt a stronger central bank response and speed the path for tightening.

items.title: Six of family killed in fire at home above grocery store in Maharashtra
points: Six members of a family — two teenage girls, their parents, and their grandparents — were killed after a fire broke out at their house above a grocery store in Maharashtra’s Dharashiv district in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026).
A boy, who was brought downstairs to safety by the parents before they went back in an effort to rescue the others, was the sole survivor.

The fire broke out around 2.30 a.m. in Yedshi village at the residence of Govind Uttam Karande (47), whose family lived on the upper floor of a building housing their grocery store, said Prakash Vhatkar, an official from the Dharashiv Revenue Office.

The deceased have been identified as Uttam Trimbak Karande (75), his wife Chandrakala Uttam Karande (70), their son Govind Uttam Karande (47), his wife Jyoti Govind Karande (42), and the couple’s daughters Gayatri (16) and Siddhi (15).

items.title: Viking Loses 1.2% in October After Eschewing Many Big AI Bets
points: (Bloomberg) -- Viking Global Investors’ flagship hedge fund dropped 1.2% last month, faring better than many of its rivals after largely avoiding high-flying artificial-intelligence stocks.
The loss pared gains for the long-short equity fund this year to about 1%, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the returns aren’t public.
The hedge fund, which manages about $35 billion, sat out tech rallies in 2020 and 2021 and avoided the double-digit losses that hit rivals.
Technology stocks made up just 7.5% of Viking’s bullish bets as of June 30, according to a regulatory filing.
Coatue Management and Tiger Global Management, for example, dedicated well over 40% of their long books to tech stocks as of June 30.
Lone Pine Capital, which erased a 44% gain it had through June, allocated more than 38% to tech.
Tiger Global’s fell 8.5% and is little changed for the year.

items.title: Oil down more than $7 a barrel in post settlement trade as Trump signals restraint on Iran
points: LONDON, - Brent crude futures continued tumbling after settlement on Monday to lose more than $7 a barrel, hitting their lowest since late August, after US President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran.
Brent crude futures settled down $5.75, or 5.85%, at $92.57 a barrel.
Prices continued falling after settlement, and were last down more than $7 a barrel.
US West Texas Intermediate futures settled down $3.98, or 4.38%, to $86.85.
US crude futures also continued falling, last down more than $5 in post-settlement trade.
The Brent benchmark plunged by 16% last week, its steepest weekly drop since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic.
On Sunday, Trump said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progressed.
Last week, Trump had hinted at a resumption of attacks on Iran and Tehran vowed to respond by striking US and Israeli targets.

items.title: Splash Crew launches to put seafarers at the heart of maritime news
points: Splash Maritime Group has unveiled Splash Crew, its latest specialist news platform, with the ambition of becoming essential daily reading for seafarers, crewing professionals, shipmanagers, regulators and maritime technology companies worldwide.
The new publication builds on Splash’s longstanding commitment to championing seafarers and examining the human side of an industry responsible for moving global trade.

The platform delivers international news, interviews, analysis and features covering crew welfare, recruitment, retention, training, safety, working conditions, regulation, career development and the rapidly changing technologies being introduced onboard…

Splash Crew is designed to bridge the gap between life onboard and decisions made ashore, bringing together perspectives from seafarers, fleet managers, crewing agencies, training institutions, technology providers and policymakers.

“At Splash, we’ve always believed that seafarers deserve far more attention than they typically receive in the maritime media,” said Sam Chambers, co-founder and editorial director of Splash Maritime Group.

items.title: G7 Launches Global Port Security Network to Combat Drug Trafficking
points: File Photo: Alexandre Tziripouloff/Shutterstock France on Monday laurched a new G7-backed network linking major seaports, customs authorities and international organizations in an effort to crack down on drug trafficking through global maritime supply chains.

The G7+ Ports Network to Combat Drug Trafficking, announced during the G7 foreign ministers’ meeting in Paris on November 9, brings together 14 ports and participating countries, including Brazil and South Korea, alongside the G7 nations.

The network was first proposed at the G7 leaders’ summit in Évian, France, in June, when leaders issued a joint declaration identifying maritime transport as the primary route for international drug and precursor chemical trafficking.

The new network will coordinate with existing initiatives, including the European Ports Alliance, and draw on international standards such as the International Maritime Organization’s International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.
According to France’s Foreign Ministry, the network is holding its first meeting in Marseille alongside the November 9–10 G7 ministerial gathering in Paris.

items.title: Ethanol blend row: Minister stands firm on claim, demands independent fuel testing
points: Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Rizwan Arshad on Monday said that he stands by the test reports on ethanol blending in petrol that were released by him on November 6.

points: TORONTO, Nov 9 (Reuters) - The Canadian dollar steadied against its US counterpart on Monday, while underperforming most other Group of 10 currencies, as oil prices fell and after recent domestic jobs data kept expectations for Bank of Canada interest rate…
US crude oil futures were trading 3.5% lower at $87.64 a barrel. * Canadian government bond yields were mixed across the curve.
The 10-year was down about half a basis point at 3.653%, after touching a nearly three-month low at 3.608% during Friday's session.

items.title: Building over Srinagar’s future
points: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah speaks in the Assembly in Srinagar on September 28, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Two conversations about the Himalayas are running at the same time, and they are not converging.
Recent notifications and bills in Jammu and Kashmir are making it easier to build more, on more land.
On a 100-square-metre plot, an FAR of 200% allows 200 square metres of floor space.
The building by-laws were amended on December 1, 2025.
On July 24, 2026, they were extended to Housing Board colonies, with additional FAR and reduced setbacks.
On September 9, fresh limits were proposed, including an FAR of 300% for commercial complexes.
On September 28, the Ease of Doing Business Bill, 2026, was tabled.
In the first week of October, the Lieutenant Governor gave his assent, and the Bill became law.

items.title: Sonia Gandhi Recalls 'Indira's Tears' Over Op Blue Star, Akali Dal Hits Back
points: A fresh political controversy has erupted in Punjab after Congress leader Sonia Gandhi reportedly wrote in her book that former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was distressed by the images emerging from Operation Blue Star, the 1984 military operation inside…

Reacting sharply to the reports, Shiromani Akali Dal spokesperson Arshdeep Singh Kler questioned the Congress leadership's expression of anguish, saying the operation was a direct attack on the Sikh community and Sri Akal Takht Sahib, the supreme temporal…
He alleged that Operation Blue Star was carried out as part of a conspiracy and said the pain of the incident would remain in the hearts of Sikhs for generations.
Drawing a parallel with the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, Kler said the pain inflicted by the Congress could not be described in words.

In an interview with "The Guardian" ahead of the release of the book, Gandhi said when her mother-in-law was shown images of the devastation during the Operation Blue Star, tears rolled down her face.

items.title: Wayanad conservationist N. Badusha wins environmental award
points: Wayanad Prakruthi Samrakshana Samithi (WPSS) president N.
Badusha has been selected for the seventh environmental award instituted by the Dr. Kamarudeen Foundation for Biodiversity Conservation (KFBC).

The award, instituted in memory of Kamarudeen, a noted environmentalist and former Reader in the Department of Botany at the University of Kerala, carries a cash prize of ₹25,000, a citation, and a plaque.
Mr. Badusha, a conservationist, is known for his efforts to protect Wayanad’s ecology and ecological heritage.

KFBC officials said this year's award was intended to recognise selfless environmental activists who had made exemplary contributions to biodiversity conservation and enhancement through their own efforts, without relying on government support or official…
In recognition of his contributions, Mr. Badusha was unanimously selected for the 2026 award, they said.
The award will be presented in a function to be held at Kariavattom in Thiruvananthapuram on November 13.

items.title: Haryana Chief Minister Attacks Bhagwant Mann Over Alleged Drinking Habit
points: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's alleged drinking habit has become a fresh political flashpoint, with both Congress and the BJP targeting him over the issue.

After Congress leader Rahul Gandhi raised the allegation at a rally in Sangrur, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini has taken a further swipe at Mann, appealing to Punjab's people to help him give up alcohol.

"Mann sahab ki daaroo chhurwao, tabhi nasha khatam ho sakta hai (make him quit drinking, then maybe the addiction can end)," Saini said, taking a dig at the Punjab Chief Minister while referring to the state's battle against drugs.

At the November 4 rally, recalling his days in Parliament with Mann, Rahul Gandhi had said, "11 baje bhi unke muh se sharab ki badbu aati thi (Even at 11 am, there was the whiff of alcohol on his breath)." "I'm not saying Bhagwant Mann should quit drinking.
But if the fight is against addiction, then the Chief Minister cannot be an addict," Gandhi had added.

items.title: Odisha cabinet approves proposal for ₹4,708-crore pumped storage project
points: Bhubaneswar, The Odisha cabinet on Monday approved 13 proposals, including a ₹4,708-crore 600 MW pumped storage project, free Wi-Fi for college students and unlimited attempts for candidates appearing in the state civil services examination till the…
The proposals were approved at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here.
"The cabinet has approved… the 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project at Ranibahal, Kalahandi district.
The state will spend a total of ₹4,708.64 crore, including ₹3,371.88 crore for construction of the project," Chief Secretary Anu Garg told reporters.
The cabinet also approved three proposals of the Water Resources Department worth ₹450 crore for in-stream storage projects and mega lift irrigation units.
In another decision, it cleared a proposal of the General Administration and Public Grievance Department to amend the Odisha Civil Services Rules, 1991.

The cabinet also approved the Odisha Shikshanet project, worth ₹393.62 crore, to provide free campus Wi-Fi with a daily limit of 1 GB across 601 colleges, benefiting around six lakh students, she said.

items.title: 2 Critical, 3 Injured After Government Buses, Car Collide In Mumbai
points: Five people sustained grievous injuries after two cars were crushed between two buses at a traffic signal in Mumbai's Colaba.
The accident took place at 9:00 pm on Monday, near the Bhakti Park traffic signal.
A BEST bus was waiting at the traffic signal.
After a few seconds, a private bus hit the last car from behind.
Police officers arrived at the location and used a crane to remove the damaged cars and buses from the road after extracting their occupants.

As per the information received from the concerned Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of LTMG Sion Hospital, at 2241 hrs, a total of five injured persons were admitted to the hospital for medical treatment," the police said in a statement.
The injured were identified as Shivani Pal (65), Pranish Pal (74), Madhupurn Pal (28), Hasharat Shaikh (34), and Balaji Pandurang Jadhav (35).

items.title: Delhi Boy Beaten To Death By Man For Bursting Crackers Near His Son
points: A 42-year-old man allegedly beat a juvenile to death with an iron rod in central Delhi's Anand Parbat area on Monday after the victim burst firecrackers close to his minor son, triggering an argument between the two minors, police said.
The incident took place at Punjabi Basti in Baljeet Nagar, where the victim was bursting firecrackers near another juvenile.
This led to a verbal spat between the two, following which the father of one of the boys intervened, a senior police officer said.
The accused, identified as Munna (42), allegedly came out of his house, picked up an iron rod and attacked the victim, the officer said.
"The argument soon escalated into a physical confrontation, following which the father of one of the juveniles allegedly intervened and attacked the other boy with an iron rod," the officer said.
The victim sustained serious injuries in the assault and was rushed to Lady Hardinge Hospital where doctors declared him brought dead, the officer said.

items.title: 6 Of Family Die As Fire Engulfs House, Attached Store On Diwali In Maharashtra
points: Six members of a family died due to severe burns and suffocation after a massive fire engulfed the family's grocery store and attached residence in Maharashtra's Dharashiv district on Diwali night.
The fire broke out at midnight and consumed the family's grocery store in Dharashiv's Yedshi village, along with their entire home, reducing everything to ashes in an instant.
The business had spanned three generations.
Two daughters of the family, Siddhi and Gayatri, who were pursuing their studies in Pune and Dharashiv, had come home to celebrate the festival and were among those who died in the incident.
Villagers are expressing deep outrage over the failure of the fire brigade to arrive on time.
Locals made desperate attempts to rescue the family trapped inside by using a JCB machine to break down the walls of the house, but by then, it was already too late.

items.title: Soldier Killed, Another Injured After Trailer Rams Army Truck In Kota
points: A havildar was killed, and a 35-year-old soldier sustained injuries after a speeding trailer collided with a stationary Army truck on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway near Jalimpura toll on Monday, police said.
The incident occurred in the Sultanpur police station area at 2.15 pm, they said.
The victim was identified as Narayan Lal (30), a native of Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, who was posted as an Army havildar in Kota.
Deepak, 35, also an Army man, sustained injuries in the collision.
According to Sultanpur SHO Daulat Sahu, Army personnel were travelling from Kota in a truck, accompanied by other Army vehicles.
The trailer, which was loaded with empty gas cylinders and travelling at a high speed, rammed into the Army truck from behind near Jalimpura - where the truck had halted, he said.
In the chaos, Lal came under the rear tyre of the truck, while Deepak was also injured.
